title: The AI Product Manager Skill Framework (2026)
source_note: Synthesized from industry write-ups (IIT Kanpur PM knowledge hub, LinkedIn practitioner guides, fonzi.ai) and live AI PM job-description analysis.

competencies.title: AI & Machine Learning Fundamentals
competencies.description: Understand supervised vs. unsupervised vs. reinforcement learning, what a neural network/transformer is, how LLMs are trained (pre-training → fine-tuning → RLHF/DPO), embeddings, and basic model-evaluation metrics (precision/recall, accuracy, perplexity, hallucination rate). This vocabulary lets you sit in a design review with ML engineers and ask the right questions.

competencies.title: Product Lifecycle Management for AI
competencies.description: AI products need continuous data pipelines, retraining, drift monitoring, and MLOps. Your PRDs need new sections: data requirements, model evaluation criteria, feedback-loop design, fallback/guardrail behavior, and a post-launch model-monitoring plan.

competencies.title: Data Literacy & Strategy
competencies.description: Understand data collection, labeling/annotation, cleaning, storage, and governance well enough to make tradeoff calls (e.g., enough labeled data to justify fine-tuning vs. RAG/prompting). Data quality is now a product requirement, not just an engineering concern.

competencies.title: Product Thinking & Strategic Vision
competencies.description: Defining the user problem, prioritizing by impact, and aligning AI capability to business outcomes — while resisting 'AI for AI's sake'. The best AI PMs kill more AI feature ideas than they ship.

competencies.title: Technical Awareness of LLM Systems
competencies.description: Practical grasp of LLM architectures conceptually, context windows, prompting vs. fine-tuning vs. RAG vs. agents, token cost/latency tradeoffs, and why outputs are probabilistic. Lets you scope realistic AI features instead of ones that only sound good in a slide.

competencies.title: Experimentation & Evaluation
competencies.description: Design experiments and build 'evals' — structured test sets that measure whether the AI is doing its job (accuracy, relevance, safety, tone). Monitor for model drift and quality regressions the same way you'd monitor uptime.

competencies.title: Ethical & Responsible AI
competencies.description: Fairness, transparency, explainability, bias mitigation, privacy, and regulatory awareness (EU AI Act, India's DPDP Act, sector rules in health/finance). Designed in at the PRD stage, not bolted on before launch.

competencies.title: Communication & Cross-functional Collaboration
competencies.description: Translate between data scientists, ML engineers, legal/compliance, and business stakeholders. Set realistic expectations about what AI can/can't do reliably, and manage the 'it demoed great, why doesn't it work in production' gap.

self_assessment: LLM/agent technical fluency (prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, agents)
